# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤞]

I can see the bomb clearly: the display reads `0`, the light is green, the button is large and labeled `PUSH TO DEFUSE`, and the wires are green, yellow, red in positions 1, 2, and 3. I cannot interpret the gestures yet because no meaning has been established for them. Mute should consult the manual and give Blind the complete tactile procedure; Blind should wait for that procedure rather than act on the button or wires.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, green light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Consult the manual and tell Blind the exact procedure. I cannot interpret the gestures yet.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb shows display 0 and a green light. It has a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Wait for Mute's manual-based instructions; do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 2

LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝]

I still see the same bomb state. Mute has sent the gestures `✌ ☝`, but no meaning has been assigned to those signs, so I cannot safely treat them as instructions. I will relay the raw signs to Blind and ask Mute to establish a clear encoding for the manual’s procedure rather than relying on an unexplained gesture sequence.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled me with gestures ✌ ☝, but their meaning is not established. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received gestures ✌ ☝ but their meaning is unknown. Establish a clear sign encoding and relay the manual's exact procedure; do not signal unexplained instructions.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. I received three gesture messages from Mute—`☝ ✌ 🤟`, `👌`, and `✌ ☝`—but gestures have no meaning until an encoding is established, and Blind cannot see them anyway. The safe communication path is for Mute to speak the manual’s instructions directly to Blind, while I continue supplying the bomb’s visible state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures ☝ ✌ 🤟, 👌, and ✌ ☝, but they have no established meaning and Blind cannot see them. Speak the manual's exact instructions directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I have received only unexplained gestures from Mute; wait for Mute's spoken manual instructions.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute’s new gestures are again unexplained; repeated patterns do not establish their meaning. Since Mute can hear me and Blind can hear both of us, Mute should state the manual’s exact rule aloud to Blind. Blind must not act based on the unlabeled gestures or on the visible button and wires alone.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Your gestures are still undefined. Speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now.")

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I now recognize the key communication route: Mute cannot speak, so Mute’s gestures reach me; I must describe those gestures aloud for Blind. I should not discard the signal as meaningless. Mute has sent a single thumbs-down gesture, which I will relay literally, while asking Mute to continue encoding the manual’s required action through gestures.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just signaled one gesture: thumbs down. The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act until the full manual instruction is conveyed.")
speak(to="mute", text="I will relay your gestures to Blind by naming them aloud. Continue sending the manual's exact instruction as a gesture sequence, and use thumbs down only if it is part of that instruction.")
wait()
```

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again sent exactly one thumbs-down gesture, 👎. This meaning is still unconfirmed; it may mean no or be part of an encoded instruction. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see repeated 👎. Blind needs the manual instruction encoded clearly. Continue with a complete gesture sequence, and I will name each gesture aloud.")

Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act on the gesture alone.")
